project_type: Cross-platform mobile application (iOS + Android), offline-first, no backend
project_description: A privacy-first personal expense tracker built with React Native (Expo SDK 53) and TypeScript, storing all data in an on-device SQLite database. Multi-currency, with annual monthly budgets, local reminder notifications, and transactional JSON import/export for device-to-device portability. Solo-authored portfolio and skills project, published to the Google Play Store and Apple App Store (user-attested).

engineering_challenges.challenge: Running one codebase on a platform where the database does not exist
engineering_challenges.why_hard: expo-sqlite has no web implementation; the alternatives are forking the data layer or blocking web entirely
engineering_challenges.solution: Structurally-typed mock SQLiteDatabase installed on Platform.OS === 'web', so every consumer is written against one interface
engineering_challenges.limitation: Web renders a functional but permanently empty app - graceful degradation, not support

engineering_challenges.challenge: Schema evolution without a migration framework
engineering_challenges.why_hard: Columns must be added to databases already on users' devices, with no server-side coordination and no way to run a one-off script
engineering_challenges.solution: Idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bootstrap; ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN wrapped in try/catch treating the already-exists error as success; backfill UPDATE for the derived column
engineering_challenges.limitation: Exception control flow in place of state; no schema version table; cannot express non-additive changes

engineering_challenges.challenge: Scheduling 'every N days' notifications on an API that supports only fixed calendar repeats
engineering_challenges.why_hard: expo-notifications offers DAILY and WEEKLY triggers; 2, 3, 14 and 30-day cadences have no native representation, and there is no server to push from
engineering_challenges.solution: Hybrid scheduler - native DAILY trigger where it fits; elsewhere a computed one-shot DATE trigger derived from last_triggered, frequency and configured time, with same-day roll-forward, written back by both tap and foreground listeners, and a blanket cancel before each reschedule
engineering_challenges.limitation: Chains can break after long inactivity; a production app would reconcile on cold start

engineering_challenges.challenge: Form state leaking across a tab navigator
engineering_challenges.why_hard: The add-expense screen serves both 'new' and 'edit'; in a tab navigator the screen stays mounted, so edit values persisted into the next new-expense entry
engineering_challenges.solution: Route-parameter identity (reset=true plus a timestamp on the tab href), a useEffect keyed on [id, reset, ts] branching between reset / load / clear, and useFocusEffect to refresh currency data on every focus
engineering_challenges.evidence: six commits over two days: b105e1c, e7ea599, 6155d3c, 921b072, 7ac750f, de49a46

engineering_challenges.why_hard: A backup file may be partially malformed; aborting the whole restore is user-hostile, but silently skipping rows can hide corruption
engineering_challenges.solution: BEGIN TRANSACTION, per-row validation across five collections, upsert by primary key, warn-and-skip malformed rows, per-collection counts returned to the caller, ROLLBACK in catch with a defensively wrapped rollback
engineering_challenges.limitation: Skipped-row counts surface only in the console, not the UI

engineering_challenges.challenge: Destructive reset that includes state outside the database
engineering_challenges.why_hard: OS-level scheduled notifications and AsyncStorage flags are not rolled back by a SQL transaction
engineering_challenges.solution: Two sequential escalating confirmations; single transaction counting then deleting 5 tables in foreign-key order; clearing the three setup flags so first-run setup re-enters correctly; cancelling all scheduled notifications

engineering_challenges.challenge: Browsing history that does not exist yet
engineering_challenges.why_hard: A new user has no data; a long-term user has years of it; the same list must serve both without loading everything
engineering_challenges.solution: Year-grouped month list from the current year, lazily appending the preceding year on onEndReached down to a floor of 2000, synthesising twelve non-interactive placeholder month cards for empty years, current month pinned and badged

decisions.title: Local-only storage, no cloud sync
decisions.problem: An expense tracker holds a detailed picture of someone's financial life; any server-side storage makes the developer custodian of that.
decisions.decision: Store everything in on-device SQLite. No backend, no account, no network transmission.
decisions.reasoning: Privacy by architecture rather than policy: data never collected cannot be breached, subpoenaed, mishandled or monetised. Also removes authentication, hosting cost, GDPR controller obligations and a large security surface from a solo-maintained app.
trade_offs: No server-side backup - device loss means data loss unless exported
No analytics, therefore no product insight and no usage metrics at all
decisions.result: A genuinely private app, and a measurable cost the author can name precisely.

decisions.title: Manual JSON export/import instead of sync
decisions.problem: Local-only storage leaves users with no way to move to a new phone.
decisions.decision: Full-database JSON export through the OS share sheet; transactional import from a picked file.
decisions.reasoning: Preserves the no-server guarantee while giving users genuine data ownership - a human-readable file they control.
decisions.result: Working device-to-device portability, documented in DATA_PORTABILITY.md.
decisions.known_issue: DATA_PORTABILITY.md describes a Merge vs Replace All choice at import; the shipped implementation offers a single upsert-by-id path. Documentation drift to correct.

decisions.title: Uniform monthly budget per year rather than per month
decisions.problem: Budgets could be per-month (flexible, 12 rows per year per currency) or one figure applied to all months.
decisions.decision: One monthly_limit per (year, currency), enforced by a UNIQUE constraint.
decisions.reasoning: Documented as a simplicity choice in BUDGET_FEATURE.md: most people hold a steady monthly target, and the simpler model makes the UI one field rather than a twelve-row editor.
trade_offs: Cannot express a seasonal or mid-year change
decisions.result: Simple model; but introduced a defect - the month list loads only the current year's budget and scores every displayed month, including earlier years, against it.

decisions.title: Denormalised currency code on expenses
decisions.problem: Expenses could reference currencies by foreign key or store the code directly.
decisions.decision: Store the ISO code string on each expense row.
decisions.reasoning: Keeps queries and the JSON export flat and self-describing; removing a currency from the user's selection cannot orphan expense rows.
trade_offs: No referential integrity between expenses and the currency table
No cascade if currency metadata changes
decisions.result: Defensible for an append-mostly local ledger keyed on a stable ISO standard, provided the cost is stated.

decisions.title: Expo managed workflow with EAS
decisions.problem: Reaching two app stores solo requires credentials, signing and build infrastructure for both platforms.
decisions.decision: Expo managed workflow with EAS Build and EAS Submit, three build profiles, remote version source, production auto-increment.
decisions.reasoning: Trades native-module freedom for a dramatically shorter path from code to signed store binary - the decision that made a solo dual-store release achievable.
decisions.result: 17+ Android build artefacts produced; both stores reached (USER-ATTESTED).

decisions.title: NativeWind for styling
decisions.problem: Styling approach for a React Native app by a developer with strong Tailwind fluency.
decisions.decision: NativeWind utility classes on seven screens.
decisions.reasoning: Rapid iteration without context-switching to a separate style object; existing Tailwind knowledge transfers directly.
trade_offs: Two screens and parts of _layout use StyleSheet.create instead, leaving an inconsistency within one codebase
decisions.result: Fast UI development; a minor cohesion weakness worth acknowledging rather than defending.

problems_solved.title: Reminder cadences the platform cannot express
problems_solved.problem: expo-notifications repeating triggers cover fixed calendar units only
problems_solved.solution: Hybrid native-daily plus computed one-shot date triggers re-armed from last_triggered
problems_solved.result: All six cadences work; remaining weakness documented

problems_solved.title: Edit form showing the previous expense
problems_solved.situation: add-expense serves both new and edit in a tab navigator
problems_solved.problem: Screen stays mounted, so state persisted across uses
problems_solved.result: Correct form state in all entry paths
problems_solved.evidence: six commits over two days in app/add-expense.tsx

problems_solved.title: Adding currency support to a schema already in use
problems_solved.situation: Multi-currency landed after the expenses table existed
problems_solved.problem: A NOT NULL column cannot be added to a populated table without a default
problems_solved.solution: ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN currency TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'GBP' in try/catch; same pattern plus backfill UPDATE for 'updated'
problems_solved.result: Backward-compatible evolution with no data loss

problems_solved.title: Browsing history that does not exist yet
problems_solved.situation: The month list must serve both a new user and one with years of data
problems_solved.solution: Lazily loaded year-grouped months with synthesised placeholders and a pinned current month
problems_solved.result: A calendar that feels complete on day one and stays navigable at scale

problems_solved.title: Apple's export-compliance gate
problems_solved.problem: Every binary must declare whether it uses non-exempt encryption or each submission stalls on a manual question
problems_solved.solution: ITSAppUsesNonExemptEncryption: false added to the iOS infoPlist - accurate, since the app performs no cryptography and makes no network calls
problems_solved.result: Submissions proceed without manual intervention; this is the final commit in the repository

known_weaknesses.issue: Zero automated tests; no runner, no test files. The pure date/currency/budget logic in lib/utils.ts is trivially unit-testable.
Budget compared across the wrong year - loadMonthlyBudget loads only the current year and the month list scores every displayed month, including earlier years, against it.
useRef called inside renderExpenseItem, a render function rather than a component - violates the Rules of Hooks and is fragile under list virtualisation.
Table name interpolated into SQL (SELECT * FROM ${table.name}). Not exploitable - names come from sqlite_master - but it is the pattern that becomes an injection when the source changes.
Exception-driven migrations with no schema version table.
Developer surfaces shipped in the release build - the debug screen is hidden via href:null rather than removed, and dev controls were commented out rather than guarded with __DEV__.
initializeDefaultCurrencies() is effectively dead code - it returns either way.
Documentation drift between DATA_PORTABILITY.md and the shipped import flow.
Artificial 500ms delay in loadMoreYears, commented as simulating database latency.
Non-daily reminder chains can break if the app is not opened for a long period.
Unused import of the deprecated ProgressBarAndroid.

lessons.lesson: Shipping is a separate skill from building.
lessons.detail: 92% of the code existed by 10 June; submission was late July. The gap was signing, icons, version codes, store metadata, review and a one-line encryption declaration. Build time does not predict ship time.

lessons.lesson: Privacy by architecture has a bill, and it comes due at review time.
lessons.detail: Choosing never to collect data is right for a personal finance app. The bill is that this dossier contains no usage metric. Knowing a decision's cost in advance is different from discovering it later.

lessons.lesson: Tab navigators do not manage your state for you.
lessons.detail: Making 'which record am I editing' explicit in the route is the durable fix; relying on mount/unmount is not.

lessons.lesson: try/catch around ALTER TABLE is where a migration strategy goes to hide.
lessons.detail: It held for two additive columns and would not survive a rename or type change. A version table and ordered migrations are a day's work at the start.

lessons.lesson: Writing the feature document alongside the feature caught design gaps.
lessons.detail: BUDGET_FEATURE.md is why the budget model's constraints are articulable today. The corollary is drift when docs are not maintained.

lessons.lesson: Skipping tests on a solo project is a loan, not a saving.
lessons.detail: The budget-year defect is the direct bill for an hour of unit tests not written.

lessons.lesson: Cross-platform means platform differences surface, not disappear.
lessons.detail: iOS cannot exit programmatically; iOS wants a spinner date picker and Android the default; web has no SQLite. The framework removes duplication, not the platforms.

high_confidence_non_quantified: Implemented a privacy-by-architecture design in which all personal financial data remains on-device - no backend, no authentication, no network transmission, no analytics - and solved the resulting portability problem with a transactional JSON export/import subsystem rather than a sync service.

requires_confirmation: Published to the App Store and Google Play, with the Android release live for over a year - currently USER-ATTESTED; settle the dates before putting them in writing.
Anything citing downloads, installs, active users or ratings - retrieve from the store consoles first. Do not estimate.
do_not_write: Any percentage, time-saving, revenue or adoption figure - none exists.
'Production system serving N users' - it is a published app with unknown usage.
'Full-stack mobile application' - there is no backend, deliberately, and the deliberateness is the better story.

interview_stories.title: The decision that cost me my metrics
interview_stories.situation: Building a personal expense tracker to publish publicly
interview_stories.task: Decide where user financial data lives
interview_stories.action: Chose on-device SQLite with no backend, account or analytics; solved device migration with transactional JSON export/import rather than a sync service
interview_stories.result: Shipped to both stores with zero user data ever transmitted - and no ability to measure usage
interview_stories.evidence: no network or analytics dependency anywhere in source; lib/dbJsonImport.ts

interview_stories.title: Working around a platform API
interview_stories.situation: Six reminder cadences required; the OS scheduler supports fixed calendar repeats
interview_stories.action: Hybrid scheduler with computed one-shot date triggers re-armed from persisted state, blanket cancel before reschedule
interview_stories.result: All six cadences work; known failure mode documented rather than hidden

interview_stories.title: Shipping is its own discipline
interview_stories.action: EAS build profiles, dependency pinning, version-code management, adaptive icons, release branch isolation, dev-control removal, iOS export compliance
interview_stories.result: Both stores; the final commit in the repository is a one-line encryption declaration six weeks after the last feature

interview_stories.title: Evolving a schema already in users' hands
interview_stories.action: Additive ALTER TABLE with sensible default, idempotent on re-run, plus backfill UPDATE
interview_stories.result: No data loss, no forced reinstall
interview_stories.honest_follow_up: It used exception control flow as a migration strategy and had no version table. It held for two additive columns and would not have held for a rename. I would start with an ordered migration runner next time.

interview_stories.title: A bug I would catch today
interview_stories.problem: The expenses screen loads only the current year's budget and compares every displayed month against it, so historical months are scored against the wrong figure
interview_stories.lesson: One unit test over budget resolution would have caught it; the project has none, a speed decision this defect is the direct bill for

interview_stories.title: Why I learn by shipping
interview_stories.situation: Not the first React Native app, but the first taken to public release
interview_stories.action: Set the goal as 'it must reach the stores', not 'it must work'
interview_stories.result: The last 10% - signing, compliance, assets, review - contained most of what was not previously known

portfolio_material.overview: A privacy-first personal expense tracker for iOS and Android, built solo with React Native and Expo. Every expense stays in a SQLite database on the user's own device.
portfolio_material.challenge: Expense trackers ask for the most sensitive data most people have. Most solve this with an account and a server, making the developer custodian of that picture. The challenge was to build something genuinely useful - multi-currency, budgeted, with reminders and device migration - without ever taking custody of a single user's data.
portfolio_material.role: Sole developer: product definition, data modelling, architecture, UI, native configuration, build pipeline, store release.
portfolio_material.solution: Offline-first architecture with a five-table SQLite schema, multi-currency domain model, uniform annual budgets with per-month progress visualisation, a hybrid local-notification scheduler, and a transactional JSON export/import subsystem answering device migration without a sync service.

audit_limitations: No production data was available or queryable, because none exists by design. This audit evaluates the artefact and its history, not its usage.
Store publication, listing duration and the visa motivation are USER-ATTESTED and were not independently verified.

The audit was performed by static inspection; the application was not built or run. Behavioural claims derive from reading the source, and the listed defects were identified by inspection rather than execution.
node_modules and package-lock.json were excluded from code metrics.
The v1-golive branch was audited; main lacks the final two release commits.
The working tree had uncommitted modifications to app.json and two asset files at audit time; these were not analysed as history.

evidence_levels_used.VERIFIED: Directly evidenced in code, configuration or Git history
evidence_levels_used.USER-ATTESTED: First-hand account from the author; not independently verifiable from the repository
evidence_levels_used.STRONGLY_SUPPORTED: Multiple pieces of evidence support the conclusion but it cannot be proven completely
evidence_levels_used.INFERRED: Appears likely based on architecture or context, but direct evidence is unavailable
evidence_levels_used.UNKNOWN: Cannot responsibly be established from available evidence
